the IGF system is altered in HIV-infected patients, with decreased IGF-I levels, increased IGFBP levels, and increased IGFBP protease activity, and that the alterations in IGFBP proteases are associated with disease progression and wasting.
the IGF-system is dysregulated in HIV infection, and the degree of the dysregulation correlates with immunological status, viral load, and clinical stage.
the IGF system is altered during HIV infection and that this alteration is related to immunological parameters as well as to the disease stage.

the relation between the immune system and the IGF system in HIV infection.

the insulin-like growth factors, IGF-I and IGF-II, and their binding proteins, IGFBP-1, IGFBP2, and IGFBP3.

IGFBP-1 and IGFBP2 are increased in HIV patients with low CD4(+) counts.
IGF-2, IGFBP- 2, and IGFBP3 proteolytic activity are altered in AIDS patients, and that the changes in IGFBP3 are correlated to the virus load.
IGF system parameters are altered in patients with HIV infection and that these changes are associated to disease progression, virus load, and clinical stage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the insulin-like growth factors are important in HIV infection, and that the alterations in the IGH system in HIV infection are related to disease progression, immunological parameters, and antireto-viral therapy.
the insulin-like growth hormone system is altered in HIV infection, and that this alteration may be of importance for disease progression and wasting.
the IGF system is altered in HIV infection and that these alterations may be of importance for the pathogenesis and progression of the disease.

the IGF system is involved in the pathophysiological processes in HIV infection, and that the IGF-IGFBPs may be used to monitor the disease course.
